✉️ Russia's Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov’s greetings to the organisers and participants of the 6th ASEAN-Russia Youth Summit (October 22, 2026)

✍️ I extend my warmest greetings to the organisers and participants of the 6th ASEAN-Russia Youth Summit, which, following a lengthy hiatus, is hosted by the hospitable and beautiful city of #Vladivostok — Russia’s Pacific outpost with a rich history and a major centre of education, science and culture.

In 2026, we mark the 35th Anniversary of relations between Russia and ASEAN, which have rightfully attained the high status of #StrategicPartnership. Our wide-ranging and robust ties bring substantial benefits to socio-economic development and serve as an important factor in maintaining regional stability.

The mutual commitment to strengthening multifaceted cooperation was clearly demonstrated at the commemorative ASEAN-Russia Summit held in Kazan this June. The Leaders devoted particular attention to creating favourable conditions to facilitate and intensify contacts among young people. 

The energy of the youth, their openness to innovation and progress are essential to ensuring progressive development of our countries and preserving an atmosphere of friendship and trust between our peoples.

The implementation of the Summit’s comprehensive agenda will also contribute to achieving these important objectives. 

It is encouraging that the programme, alongside thematic discussions and round tables, features an extensive cultural component.

🤝 I wish you all fruitful work, positive impressions of your stay in the Russian land of #Primorye and every success.

SERGEY LAVROV

#RussiaASEAN

Russia delivers 125.9 tonnes of humanitarian food aid to Laos.

On October 20, Russian Ambassador to Laos Sergey Zhestkyi attended a ceremony in Luang Namtha marking the handover of another shipment of Russian humanitarian assistance.

As part of Russia's contribution to the UN World Food Programme (#WFP), 125.9 tonnes of food supplies were delivered to Laos through the Russian Emergencies Ministry, including 79 tonnes of canned fish and 46.9 tonnes of sunflower oil. The aid will be distributed to communities affected by severe flooding, including those in Luang Namtha Province.

In 2025, Russia provided Laos with another 318 tonnes of food supplies to support school feeding programmes in the country's northern provinces.

🤝 Ambassador Sergey Zhestkyi stressed that Russia's humanitarian assistance to friendly Laos forms an important part of joint efforts to address the consequences of natural disasters and contributes to the country's socio-economic development.
